sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL IS COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY,
 JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:17999  MFA No. 20770 of 2013  JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the insured of the offending vehicle challenging the judgment and award dated 09.11.2012 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Sirsi, in MVC No.62/2011.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 29.01.2011 at about 12:00 noon, on Ramanabial road, when the claimant was riding his Baja M-80 scooter bearing registration No.KA-31-H-8931 towards his house, the driver of autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-31-4036 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his scooter resulting in the petitioner sustaining multiple grievous injures.

He was shifted to P.G.
Hospital, Sirsi and later was shifted to TSS Hospital, Sirsi, where he NC: 2024:KHC-D:17999 underwent surgery.
Hence, the claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.
3. Upon service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and filed their objections denying the averments made in the claim petition.
4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the petition against respondent No.1 awarding compensation of Rs.97,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment and dismissed the petition by exonerating the respondent-insurance company from paying the compensation.
Being aggrieved, present appeal has been filed by respondent No.1/owner of the offending vehicle.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant/owner of the offending vehicle contended that, at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding a NC: 2024:KHC-D:17999 valid and effective driving licence to drive LMV non- transport.

He further contended that in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance company Sri. Micheal Lorrence Dsouza vs Mohammad Akbar S/O : Mohammad Salia Khan on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39177165/
2 Limited1 the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid driving licence to drive the transport vehicle as the unladen weight of the vehicle is less than 7500kg but the Tribunal erred in fastening the liability on the owner of the offending vehicle by exonerating the insurance company.

sentences.text: Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal by setting aside the judgment passed by the Tribunal.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel for insurance company contended that, admittedly, as on the date of the accident, though the driver of the offending vehicle was holding LMV non-transport driving licence, he was driving a transport vehicle and thereby has violated the policy conditions.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly exonerated.

AIR 2017 SUPREME COURT 3668 NC:
2024:KHC-D:17999 the insurance company from satisfying the compensation.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned judgment and award and the original records.
8.

It is not in dispute that the claimant has suffered injuries in a road traffic accident occurred on 29.01.2011 due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the autorickshaw bearing registration No. KA-31-4036.
It is also not in dispute that the driver of the offending vehicle was holding driving licence to drive non-transport vehicle but he drove a transport vehicle.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra), has held that, 'driver holding LMV licence can drive all vehicles of class including transport vehicles if the unladen weight does not exceed 7500kg and no separate endorsement is required to drive such transport vehicles".
In the case on hand, the unladen weight of the vehicle is less than NC: 2024:KHC-D:17999 7500kg and hence, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
The Tribunal has erred in exonerating the insurance company from satisfying the compensation.
Hence, the following order.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The judgment 09.11.2012 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Sirsi, in MVC No.62/2011 is modified.
Insurance company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
Registry is directed to refund the amount in deposit, if any, in favour of the appellant after due identification.
